question: A 64-year-old man presents with a complaint of prominent stiffness in his legs which is causing a difficulty in ambulation. He is not able to relax his trunk area and has frequent, painful muscle spasms. He denies diplopia, swallowing difficulties, and urinary or bowel problems. He has a medical history of stage IV lung cancer. He has received 4 sessions of chemotherapy. The neurological examination reveals an increased generalized muscle tone. He has a spastic gait with exaggerated lumbar lordosis. The needle electromyography (EMG) studies show continuous motor unit activity that persists at rest. Which paraneoplastic antibody is most likely associated with the symptoms of this patient?
reasoning_chain: CHAIN: "Stage IV lung cancer" -> "Paraneoplastic syndrome possible" -> "Neurological symptoms manifest" -> "Increased generalized muscle tone" -> "Spastic gait with exaggerated lumbar lordosis" -> "Continuous motor unit activity at rest" -> "Anti-Hu antibody most likely associated" -> 85%

CHAIN: "Chemotherapy sessions" -> "Potential trigger for paraneoplastic syndrome" -> "Neurological symptoms develop" -> "Increased generalized muscle tone" -> "Spastic gait with exaggerated lumbar lordosis" -> "Continuous motor unit activity at rest" -> "Anti-Hu antibody most likely associated" -> 80%
analysis: The patient's presentation of stiffness in the legs, muscle spasms, and increased muscle tone with a spastic gait is suggestive of a paraneoplastic syndrome. Given his history of stage IV lung cancer and the specific symptoms described, the most likely paraneoplastic antibody associated with these symptoms is Anti-Hu (option b). Anti-Hu antibodies are commonly associated with paraneoplastic neurological syndromes in patients with small cell lung cancer.
